# 🎬 Media Bar Arrives on Jellyfin 12

Media Bar **3.0.0.0** brings support for **Jellyfin 12**, including compatibility with both the classic desktop experience and Jellyfin's newer modern web layout.

> ## 🙌 Huge thanks to MakD and the upstream contributors
>
> Media Bar itself is the work of **MakD and the contributors to the upstream Media Bar project**. The plugin I maintain is primarily a Jellyfin wrapper around that work, exposing configuration and integration points so it can be installed and managed cleanly as a Jellyfin plugin.
>
> A huge amount of effort has gone into keeping Media Bar working across Jellyfin's changing web interface, especially for Jellyfin 12. The features, UI work and frontend improvements in this release are built on that upstream work, and the credit for that belongs to **MakD and everyone contributing there**.
>
> My part is largely packaging, integrating and exposing that work through Jellyfin's plugin system.

## ✨ New Features

* Added support for **Jellyfin 12**.
* Added support for Jellyfin 12's **modern React/MUI home screen layout**, alongside the existing classic desktop layout.
* Updated the bundled Media Bar frontend to the latest Jellyfin 12-compatible upstream version.
* Added Jellyfin 12-specific styling so Media Bar integrates correctly with the new web-client shell while retaining the existing appearance on the classic layout.
* Media Bar continues to ship its frontend assets directly with the plugin, ensuring the version displayed in Jellyfin matches the plugin version you've installed.

## 🛠️ Improvements

* Synced Media Bar with the latest Jellyfin 12-compatible upstream work.
* Improved Media Bar placement within the Jellyfin 12 home screen across both supported layouts.
* Improved layout behaviour on taller displays, ensuring Jellyfin's home-screen rows remain below the Media Bar content rather than overlapping its controls.
* Improved localisation handling when loading Jellyfin's translation chunks.
* Retained support for the **Get updates early** option for users who explicitly want to track unreleased upstream Media Bar changes.

## 🪲 Bug Fixes

* Fixed Media Bar being inserted in the wrong position when using Jellyfin 12's modern layout (#181).
* Fixed translated Media Bar strings falling back to English or producing JSON decoding errors for some languages (#185).
* Fixed home-screen rows overlapping Media Bar buttons on taller viewports.
* Fixed Jellyfin 12 layout differences that could cause Media Bar to render incorrectly compared with Jellyfin 10.11.

## ⚠️ Compatibility

* **Media Bar 3.0.0.0 supports Jellyfin 10.11.11 and Jellyfin 12.**
* Users on older Jellyfin 10.x versions should remain on a compatible **2.x** Media Bar release.
* Jellyfin 12 support includes both the **classic Desktop layout** and the newer **modern React/MUI layout**.
* A compatible **File Transformation 3.x** release is required.
* If you're using the **Get updates early** option, unreleased upstream Media Bar changes may behave differently from the frontend bundled and tested with this plugin release.

## Contributors

* austinnorgaard
* judarange

## ❤️ Support

If you enjoy using my Jellyfin plugins and want to support the time that goes into building, maintaining, and improving them, you can do so on [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/IAmParadox27).

Thank you for using the plugins and being part of the community.

v3.0.1.2 - Discovery background work respects its master switch, Trakt travels with backup

- Seerr discovery generation and the Trakt refresh no longer run while Discovery user access is off; stored choices resume automatically on re-enabling
- Backup export/import round-trips the "Enable Trakt discovery" flag, so the choice survives a move to a fresh installation
- The Trakt checkbox only appears with Discovery on and the official Trakt plugin detected, and auto-saves like the Discovery toggle
- DryRun warms discovery caches without persisting, and leaves the shared trending pool untouched
- Greyed-out settings are now truly inert (keyboard and screen readers), and unsaved-changes tracking no longer reports phantom edits
- Tested by 6800 unit tests and 369 end-to-end tests
- Requires Jellyfin 12.2 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6

v3.0.1.1 - "Trakt for you" no longer stays empty; discovery is quieter and self-healing

- Fixed the main report: "Trakt for you" could stay empty while trending and the local picks were full. Virtual stub library entries (real-looking files with a TMDb id but no media, created by some request helpers) were counted as owned and silently excluded every personal pick. They are now recognised as virtual and ignored, so your Trakt recommendations come through
- An empty "Trakt for you" is no longer sticky: a null or empty result is cached only briefly, so once the server has your picks they appear on the next open instead of being held behind a stale empty view
- A rate-limited or unreachable Trakt is retried with a backoff (honouring the server's Retry-After) instead of being re-hit on every tab load, and the same account open on two devices now shares one fetch instead of firing two
- An unlinked user no longer sees a "Trakt for you" tab that only shows a not-linked message; the tab appears once you are linked, and "Trakt trending" (which needs no login) is always available
- The plugin log now explains an empty personal result in one line (what was fetched, what survived, and why), so a token, fetch, or ownership issue is far easier to pin down
- Tested by 6779 unit tests and 369 end-to-end tests
- Requires Jellyfin 12.2 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6
- Special thanks to @TheColin21 (https://github.com/TheColin21) for finding and reporting the empty "Trakt for you" issue and for debugging it together ❤️

v3.0.1.0 - Trakt discovery + encrypted secrets, Discovery tab no longer goes blank on Jellyfin 12

- New Trakt discovery source: when the official Jellyfin Trakt plugin is installed, the Discovery tab gains two sub-tabs beside the local picks, "Trakt for you" (your personal Trakt recommendations) and "Trakt trending" (global, no login), using the same card layout, request/dismiss mechanics, and per-user ML scoring. The Helper has no Trakt app of its own: it sources everything read-only through the official plugin's connection, so there is nothing to configure per user and no second app to register. A single "Enable Trakt discovery" checkbox (shown only when the official plugin is detected) turns it on
- All stored credentials (Seerr and Arr API keys) are now encrypted at rest with Data Protection and never logged in plain text; backups stay portable and re-encrypt on restore
- The Seerr Discovery custom tab reliably shows its content again on Jellyfin 12: navigating away and back no longer leaves it blank
- Returning to the tab is instant and never flashes a spinner: the last results render immediately from memory, and newer suggestions are swapped in silently in the background when a scheduled run has produced them
- The sidebar "Seerr Discovery" link opens the tab correctly on the modern Jellyfin 12 layout (both the top header and the narrow-screen menu), as well as on the classic layout
- The Codecs tab cards can now be rearranged by dragging a card's header handle (long-press on touch, with edge auto-scroll) or by keyboard (Enter to grab, arrow keys to move, Enter to drop, Escape to cancel); the order saves instantly, survives refresh/restart/update, and travels with backup export/import
- Radarr/Sonarr instances behind a reverse proxy with a private CA, self-signed, or IP certificate can now connect via a per-instance "Skip certificate validation" checkbox in Settings
- Recommendations now follow completed franchises: a series you finished years ago is surfaced again when a new entry arrives, instead of being outranked by whatever you watched most recently
- Recommendation explanations are now concrete: the "Why" line names what actually drove the pick (completing a collection, a franchise, a matched writer/country/era, or genuine crowd popularity) instead of a vague "Recommended for you". Discovery suggestions keep their person/genre/trending/popularity reasons, now with an honest fallback instead of claiming "Popular and highly rated" for a title that is neither
- Hardening: API keys, the log filter, and backup credentials now reject hidden control characters that could cause errors or log tampering; odd-charset responses are read safely; and restoring a backup that disables TLS validation now warns you first
- Recommendation playlists are always private: playlist sync now sets visibility explicitly instead of relying on the server default, so each user's recommendations stay visible to that user only
- Tested by 6720 unit tests (expanded security, hardening, and performance coverage) and 368 end-to-end tests
- Requires Jellyfin 12.2 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6
- Special thanks to @TheColin21 (https://github.com/TheColin21) for testing and donation ❤️
- Special thanks to Daniel for his donation ❤️
- Special thanks to @baervers23 (https://github.com/baervers23) for great input and ideas ❤️

v3.0.0.4 - Per-library file counts, boxset link fix

- The Per-Library Breakdown now shows a file count below every size value (trickplay folders included), so sparse and dense libraries are distinguishable at a glance
- Boxset library rows no longer link into the Library Explorer, whose scope excludes boxsets; they render as plain text instead of opening an empty state
- Every task dropdown in Settings now explains what the task does, via an info button next to each task name, in all dashboard languages
- The Overview Trickplay card now also shows the space used by trickplay images Jellyfin stores internally, on its own line below the alongside-media total, marked with an (internal) badge, or as the headline when no alongside data exists
- Compact log view on phones: log entries stack as cards below 700 px instead of squeezing into a four-column table, so no horizontal scrolling is needed, and rows keep breathing room at the screen edges
- Roomier Library Explorer filter popovers on phones using nearly the full viewport width, like the bitrate editor
- Tested by 6219 unit tests and 352 end-to-end tests
- Requires Jellyfin 12.1 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6

v3.0.0.3 - Library Explorer, new Codecs breakdowns, disabled users ignored

- The Codecs tab now has a Library Explorer: combine resolution, codecs, bitrate, languages, watched users and formats into one search, scoped to the libraries you pick in its multi-select, so you can find e.g. all 4K films with low bitrate
- Options with zero matches under the other filters are hidden automatically, dimensions without matches stay greyed out, and multi-value dropdowns accept several audio languages, subtitle languages or users at once
- Every active filter is shown in the result header and a Reset button clears the whole search; results arrive as the familiar grouped file tree with Movies, TV Shows and other sections
- Jump straight into the search from the Overview: each library name and all four media cards open the Explorer pre-filtered to that scope
- Every categorical filter can be negated with Includes/Excludes, so you can search e.g. audio languages that are not German; excluded picks show as ≠ pills and counts preview what stays
- Four new breakdowns in the Codecs tab, each with drill-down to the exact files: Video Bitrate (7 tiers from < 2 to > 60 Mbps), Audio Languages, Subtitle Languages and Watched (by username plus Never watched)
- Each bitrate tier uses what Jellyfin measured for the video stream; when a file has no per-stream value the average is estimated from its size and runtime, so almost every file lands in a real tier instead of Unknown
- Disabled Jellyfin users no longer skew results: their old plays are excluded from Smart Recommendations, watch history and the new Watched breakdown
- Long breakdowns start collapsed behind a Show-all toggle with Unknown always last, and unreadable language tags fold into Unknown instead of junk entries
- Added responsive, independently scrollable library result cards.
- Improved compact layouts for mobile controls.
- Added consistent themed scrollbar styling across plugin panels and lists.
- The Overview Per-Library Breakdown has a new Other column per library covering NFO files, text files and other unrecognized sidecar files, plus a Books column whenever a book library exists, so every row adds up exactly to its Total
- Tested by 6169 unit tests and 341 end-to-end tests
- Requires Jellyfin 12.1 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6

v3.0.0.2 - Log tab, save bar, resolution and touch fixes

- Clearing the plugin log no longer briefly shows a false "Failed to clear logs." error: the Clear button now confirms success immediately and refreshes the view right away
- Genuine clear failures (e.g. expired session or server error) now write a structured diagnostic to the browser console with the HTTP status and error kind, alongside the visible red button feedback, so a real problem is never silent
- Save bar no longer crowds on phones: the unsaved-changes label and Save button now stack on narrow screens, so long translations like the German "Nicht gespeichert" are no longer cut off
- Widescreen films are counted at their real resolution: cinemascope masters like 1920x800 or 1920x1040 are now correctly shown as 1080p instead of 720p in the Codecs tab, decided by whichever axis reaches a resolution class
- The resolution drill-down now lists each file's exact pixel dimensions (e.g. 1920x800) next to its name, readable on desktop and phones
- Chart tooltips work reliably on touch: the first tap on the Trends chart or a Codecs ring now shows and keeps the tooltip instead of flashing it away, and a second tap on the same Codecs segment closes it
- The save confirmation only appears after a real save: reverting a setting back to its original value no longer briefly shows "All changes saved"
- Tested by 5535 unit tests and 320 end-to-end tests
- Requires Jellyfin 12.0 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6

v3.0.0.1 - Per-instance library allocation for Arr

- Assign specific Jellyfin libraries to each Radarr/Sonarr instance, so the Arr tab compares an instance only against the libraries it manages
- With two or more instances of a type, each gets a picker in Settings listing only the matching kind of library (movies for Radarr, TV for Sonarr)
- Leave a picker empty to keep it automatic: instances are matched to libraries from their root folders
- Assignments are kept across backup and restore
- Fixes a 4K instance flagging every 1080p film as "not in Radarr"
- Tested by 5499 unit tests and 318 end-to-end tests
- Requires Jellyfin 12.0 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6

v3.0.0.0 - Major release for Jellyfin 12.0+

- Books in your library overview: eBook libraries now show their size and file count on the Overview tab and count towards your storage totals, and they're always protected from every cleanup task
- Smarter recommendations: a much bigger model, fairer suggestions for brand-new users, and more variety in your top picks (no more ten near-identical films in a row)
- Recommendations now also learn from franchises/collections, country of origin, collection & folder themes, whether a series is finished or ongoing, writers/creators, top-billed cast, and how rare a genre or studio is in your library (each signal is optional per item, so missing metadata never skews a pick)
- Fresh picks appear between nightly runs, and faster generation on big libraries
- Redesigned Settings, Health and Arr tabs with a live 'reachable' indicator, plus a sticky save bar and unsaved-changes warning
- Better on phones
- Stronger security: API keys are never shown to the browser, backups can leave keys out, and cleanup can never delete or touch anything outside your media libraries
- Safer trash and cleanup: turning retention off really turns it off, trashing a shortcut never removes the file it points to, and Windows shortcut handling is fixed
- More accurate library stats and safer Seerr request cleanup
- More reliable saves and backups (no more rare 'lost save' when antivirus is scanning)
- New end-to-end test suite runs the plugin inside a real Jellyfin 12 server on every change and proves cleanup stays inside your libraries
- Note: your recommendation model retrains from scratch after upgrading, so suggestions settle back in over the next scheduled runs
- Requires Jellyfin 12.0 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6

AniList come fonte senza chiave insieme a TMDB: cast giapponese con i personaggi, studio di animazione, date, stato, voto, trailer, copertina e banner, solo nei campi vuoti. L'anno di una stagione senza date arriva dalla catena dei sequel di AniList, se gli episodi coincidono. Gli ID AniList che non corrispondono per tipo o anno vengono ignorati. Nuovo passo AniList nel setup. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

Comunità per tutti: dopo una correzione il plugin chiede se condividerla e la invia tramite il servizio della comunità, senza account; il token GitHub diventa facoltativo. Si condividono anche le stagioni con una scheda propria, applicate agli altri solo se numero di stagione ed episodi coincidono. Elenco approvato aggiornato ogni giorno, controlli automatici e approvazione con un'etichetta, tessera Comunità in Inizio, passo Comunità nel setup e scelta della stagione in «Correggi un abbinamento». Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

Pagina del plugin rifatta da zero con l'identità di AnimeClick: setup guidato al primo avvio e solo i passi nuovi dopo gli aggiornamenti importanti, vetrina degli ultimi anime aggiornati, cruscotto della collezione, libreria a locandine con titoli e trame uniti per anime, attivazione delle librerie a un clic e ricerca della scheda su AnimeClick per correggere un abbinamento. Corretti i conteggi dell'analisi di una singola serie, lo stato della condivisione comunitaria appena attivata e «Da verificare», che ora coincide con quanto «Sistema tutti i titoli» ricontrolla. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

AnimeClick come unico provider remoto per le librerie anime: identificazione TMDB verificata, completamento dei metadati senza altri plugin e immagini integrate Fanart → TMDB → AnimeClick. Chiavi Fanart personale e di progetto nelle impostazioni, con link e verifica. Numerazione, campi bloccati e immagini esistenti conservati. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

AnimeClick primo campo per campo: i valori generici lasciano spazio alle fonti configurate. Requests og Kalender i burger-menuen.

Når Jellyfin 12 kører med den gamle skuffe - f.eks. med New Badges' burger-knap
på brede skærme - lægges de to links nu også ind der, lige under Hjem. Menuen
lukker af sig selv, når man klikker på dem.

Styres af de indstillinger, der allerede findes (Requests-fanen og
Kalender-fanen). Ingen nye indstillinger.

Kun Jellyfin 12.

- Menupillen øverst findes nu også i et halvt vindue: ikoner, med navnet på den side du er på, og et hint på resten. På en telefon ligger alt i menuen som før.
- Den valgte knap i pillen er hvid i stedet for blå.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.2.2.0.

Hele topbaren i én knapgruppe på Jellyfin 12.

- Film, Serier og dine andre biblioteker er nu med i knapgruppen, efter Favoritter og før Tilføj og Kalender. Før stod de uden for, så gruppen så ud som en bar, der stoppede halvvejs.
- Det bibliotek, du er inde i, er fyldt ud i gruppen.
- Ingen tynd kant rundt om gruppen længere - over banneret lignede den en rest af den gamle topbar. Gruppen har nu en mørk, let sløret baggrund i stedet.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.2.2.0.

Ny topbar på Jellyfin 12.

- Hjem, Favoritter, Tilføj og Kalender er samlet i én knapgruppe, hvor den side, du er på, er fyldt ud. Før var Hjem slet ikke med, og den aktive side blev kun vist med blå tekst.
- Kortere navne: "Tilføj" og "Kalender" (på engelsk "Request" og "Calendar"), så topbaren også er plads til på en bærbar.
- Tilføj og Kalender virker nu også fra andre sider end forsiden - før skete der ingenting.
- Rettet: efter at have åbnet Kalender kunne både Tilføj og Kalender stå markeret, og i sidemenuen på mobilen kunne tre punkter være markeret på én gang.
- Rettet: at skifte fra Tilføj eller Kalender til Hjem eller Favoritter kunne vise to faner oven i hinanden.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.2.2.0.

Forsiden indlæses hurtigere.

- Kalenderens hukommelse - alle de titler, den har set - ligger nu i sin egen fil på serveren i stedet for i plugin-indstillingerne. Indstillingerne hentes af alle browsere ved hver sideindlæsning og var vokset til over 100 KB; nu er de få KB. Flytningen sker af sig selv, når serveren starter.
- Scriptet caches af browseren og hentes kun igen, når plugin'et er opdateret.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.2.2.0.

Udgivelseskalenderen viser ikke længere gamle film som Point Break og The Godfather.

TMDB registrerer hver gang en film bliver vist på tv eller lagt på en streamingtjeneste - i alle lande. Kalenderen tog den første dato den fandt, så en fransk tv-visning af Point Break fra 1991 dukkede op som en kommende udgivelse. Nu gælder:

- Film der allerede ligger i biblioteket, vises ikke i kalenderen.
- Kalenderen bruger den tidligste streamingdato, ikke den første der står på listen.
- En dato mere end to år efter filmens premiere er en genudgivelse og vises ikke.

Til Jellyfin 12.

"Test forbindelse"-knappen ser nu rigtig ud ved siden af Gem.

Efter sidste udgave var Gem-knappen tegnet om til Jellyfin 12's stil, men "Test forbindelse" lige under den sad tilbage i den gamle grå udgave, så de to knapper så ud til at være lige vigtige.

Den er nu en omridset knap i temaets farve — samme størrelse som Gem, men tydeligt den sekundære af de to, præcis som Jellyfin 12 selv tegner et sådant knappepar.

Kun udseende. Knappen gør nøjagtig det samme som før.

Indstillingssiden er tegnet om, så den ser ud som resten af Jellyfin 12.

Jellyfin 12 har lavet sine egne indstillingssider om: felterne er nu fyldte bokse med en lille etiket øverst i selve feltet, i stedet for en label ovenover. Denne side fulgte stadig den gamle stil og stak derfor ud fra alt andet i dashboardet.

Felter, afkrydsningsfelter, overskrifter og Gem-knappen matcher nu Jellyfin 12's egne — samme højde, samme afrunding, samme farver. Farverne hentes fra Jellyfin 12's eget tema, så siden også følger med hvis du skifter tema.

Kun udseende. Der er ikke ændret noget i hvad siden gør, eller i indstillingerne selv. På Jellyfin 10.11 ser siden ud præcis som før — den nye stil slås kun til, hvis serveren rent faktisk er 12.

Understøtter nu Jellyfin 12.

Fanerne "Tilføj Film/Serie" og "Udgivelseskalender" er flyttet med. Jellyfin 12 har lavet hele den øverste menulinje om, og den gamle fanerække findes stadig i siden men bliver aldrig tegnet — så fanerne blev lagt et sted ingen kunne se dem. De sidder nu i den rigtige menulinje sammen med Favoritter, Film og Serier, og i menuen i siden på telefon.

Jellyfin 12 afviser den gamle måde at sende adgangsnøglen på (X-Emby-Token), så alle kald bruger nu det almindelige Authorization-felt. Uden det svarede serveren 401.

Indstillingssiden kunne ikke åbnes på Jellyfin 12. Pluginet kørte, men dets side under Dashboard → Plugins var der ikke, og der stod ingen fejl nogen steder. Jellyfin 12's nye dashboard viser kun siden, hvis den selv beder om at komme i menuen.

Accentfarven læses nu direkte fra temaet. Før blev den gættet ved at male en usynlig knap med Jellyfins egne klasser og aflæse farven — men Jellyfin 12 tegner sine knapper på en ny måde hvor den klasse ikke findes, så gættet slog fejl og faldt tilbage til en fast farve.

Denne udgave er bygget til Jellyfin 12 og kan kun installeres der. Kører du stadig 10.11, bliver du på den forrige udgave, som virker uændret — serveren vælger selv den rigtige. Grunden til at der skal være to: 10.11 og 12 kører på hver sin udgave af .NET, så det samme build kan ikke køre begge steder.

versions.changelog:
Hotfix for 1.0.8.0 — the Issues tab went blank and unresponsive on servers with substantial history.

Root cause: the new per-row "last attempt" lookup in 1.0.8.0 ran a correlated subquery against the history table with no supporting index. On loaded databases the query stalled long enough that Jellyfin tore down the request scope mid-flight, which crashed MVC's result serializer with ObjectDisposedException — the Issues tab silently rendered empty and every button that depended on live issue data felt dead.

Schema v11 adds a covering index on history(issue_id, dry_run, fixed_at_utc). Non-destructive migration: SQLite builds the index from existing rows. No rescan, no history loss, no re-queue needed.

Measured ~450x speed-up on the correlated query (approx 5000ms -> approx 15ms per 500-id chunk on a 48k-row history), and GET /MediaDash/Issues?openOnly=true now returns a steady HTTP 200 instead of timing out and 500ing. 1526 / 1526 tests green.

Fixes #80.

Protection: right-click (or long-press) in the Files tab to protect any file/folder from scans and fixes, or push one into the issue queue.

"Original language" option added to audio/subtitle pickers. (#78)

Format converters for images, music and video (RMVB → MKV), with a first-run wizard step to enable them.

SMART monitoring is disable-able per server via right-click on the SMART pill. (#60)

Per-fixer disable toggle in Settings → Fix order.

Playability: catches damaged secondary audio tracks; books and comics refused with a doc-aware message; audio files with cover art no longer false-flagged. (#75, #76)

Repair + conversion safety: source identity captured before encoding, output verified against source duration/stream count, audiobook merges won't overwrite an existing .m4b. Alternate audio tracks preserved on RMVB → MKV remuxes.

Scanning: Photos library now covered; Overview breakdown includes Music/Books/Photos; `.txt` books aren't flagged as orphans; respects Enabled Libraries setting.

Cross-volume moves refuse symlinks/junctions and verify inventory before deleting the source.

Many UI fixes across Issues tab, Settings, Overview and Recycle. "Reset scan data" preserves Queued/Dismissed decisions.

Light-mode: Files-tab right-click menu and Protect dialog are now readable under the Light theme.

Calibre: no longer hangs on verbose installers; paths with spaces work; override path changes picked up without restart.

Hotfix for 1.0.7.6 Playability false-positives.

• Removed the bitrate-vs-size pre-filter that flagged efficient x264 rips (YIFY / small MP4 rips of Severance / Landman / Rage / Outlander at 400 MB–2.4 GB) as size-truncated. Decode-check already catches genuine tail-truncation with far fewer false positives.

• DRM detection: encrypted MP4/M4V/M4A/MOV (Fairplay / Widevine / PlayReady) detected via codec_tag_string=encv/enca and skipped instead of mis-flagged.

• Folder-based library items (BDMV / VIDEO_TS / mounted-ISO / BDRemux) no longer reported as missing files.

Anyone on 1.0.7.6 should update — the 1.0.7.6 repair ladder would try to salvage these false positives and recycle files that failed repair.

753 / 753 tests green. 15 / 15 real-file torture-test variants still recover end-to-end.

Repair broken files ladder (quick remux → drop broken streams → container coerce → re-encode) + F-014/015/016 malformed-row robustness sweep (dashboard, PlayabilityFixer, HasBlockingWarnings + 6 other JSON readers hardened) + Media Grouper year-suffix fix for TV reboots (#43 Doctor Who, Silo) + Track fix VobSub/PGS/DVB consent gate for MP4-family (#56) + Track/Playability/Transcode fixers widened to UnauthorizedAccessException on SMB/NFS/FUSE (#59) + Recycle bin 5 GB soft-warn for Proxmox LXC / Docker bind-mount (#58) + Errors tab: correct labels for pauses / skips / malformed-row / ffmpeg-on-corrupt-source + stable FNV-1a dedup + 10-minute review grace + plain-language messages everywhere.

753 / 753 tests green. 15 / 15 real-file torture-test variants recover end-to-end. One binary for Jellyfin 10.11 and 12.0.
Fix window + Low system impact mode + HW-accelerated re-encodes + Show ignored issues + one-per-session fix-run alert + midnight scan default + Media Grouper collision guard + Errors badge accuracy

1.0.7.4 is a small follow-up to 1.0.7.3's combined audio + subtitle cleanup pass, closing the last case where MediaDash could ffmpeg the same file twice in one fix run.

When a file had a queued re-encode AND queued track cleanup (unwanted audio or subtitle languages), it used to remux for the tracks first and then re-encode a second time. The re-encode already drops unwanted tracks by itself, so the first remux was wasted work — and if it didn't run first, it would fail with "nothing to remove" once the re-encode had finished. Now the fix run detects the overlap and lets the re-encode handle both jobs in one pass. Same recycle bin entry, one history row per issue, both track and quality issues flip to Fixed together.

User-visible impact: multi-language 4K remuxes that also need size reduction finish in half the time, and the Errors tab stops picking up spurious "nothing to remove" failures on files that were just re-encoded.

594 / 594 tests green. One binary for Jellyfin 10.11 and 12.0.

1.0.7.3 addresses the loudest bug reports from GitHub issues and the r/jellyfin + r/JellyfinCommunity threads.

Recycle bin: overhauled with rich per-row metadata (BinPath, Provenance, Reason, IssueType, ActionText, RestoreHint, auto-purge countdown), origin-manifest sidecars so restores survive history loss, cross-volume consolidation of legacy bin locations, non-destructive restore that suffixes -restored instead of overwriting, and a 3 GB / 5 GB free-space floor that pauses fix runs and refuses config save on a full bin volume. New endpoints: /RecycleBin/OtherBins, /RecycleBin/Consolidate, /RecycleBin/DiskInfo.

Duplicate detection: keys now include ProductionYear so remakes stop collapsing (#3), keeper picker excludes symlinks and 0-byte files (F-098), DuplicateMinAgeDays default 7 to 0 with one INFO line naming vetoed count.

Fixer output: TrackFixer + TranscodeFixer restore source CreationTimeUtc and LastWriteTimeUtc so Recently-Added stays honest (#31); dry-run stale-failure path no longer flips vanished files to Fixed; per-sidecar history fan-out via FixResult.AdditionalRecycled gives every recycled sidecar its own Restore button; subtitle-provider quota mid-run is now detected and handled quietly.

Playability: cross-checks ffprobe format_name against extension so an MKV renamed .mp3 emits container-extension-mismatch (F-213). HasTruncationMarker no longer treats the benign Truncating packet warning as truncation - that warning fires on real-world MKV cluster boundaries, MPEG-TS packet alignment, and MP4 mdat overlap on files that play fine in Jellyfin (Reddit reports: friskyapple, oogoom, moonplaza, Commercial-Camp-8052). Only File ended prematurely now counts.

TrackFixer ffmpeg command gains -fflags +genpts at input and -avoid_negative_ts make_zero at output - fixes the mpegts sample rate not set / Could not write header failure on Blu-ray-derived .m2ts sources, and lets OutputVerifier accept legitimate long-form duration drift (#39, slack widened from fixed 2 s to max(2 s, dur x 2 percent)).

Combined ffmpeg pass (#28, #32): FixTask now detects same-file AudioLanguage + SubtitleLanguage pairs before the fix loop and routes them through a new TrackFixer.FixCombinedAsync so one ffmpeg drops both categories in a single pass instead of two back-to-back remuxes. Two history rows recorded, one bin entry, both issues flip to Fixed.

SMART noise dedup: SmartHealthProbeWmi caches per-drive-letter WMI failures and SmartHealthProbe caches per-device smartctl timeout / IO / non-zero-exit failures. First failure per device per session still emits the diagnostic; subsequent failures on the same device are suppressed until restart. Addresses the Errors-tab spam on NVMe + mount-point setups (#38, #23).

Files: new read-only Jellyfin logs shortcut at the file-browser root supporting listing + per-file download so users can attach logs to bug reports; ApiKey= param renamed from api_key= for Jellyfin 10.10+ compatibility.

Diagnostics: Copy diagnostics button relabelled Report an issue (copies diagnostics + opens issue tracker in a new tab).

Reliability hotfix: fixes the "13 files locked, nothing holding them" report class by switching every scanner/probe (ArtworkScanner, NfoScanner, TrickplayOptimizeScanner, BookProbeService, FileHasher) from File.OpenRead (default FileShare.Read blocks concurrent moves/deletes on Windows and shows up as ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION 32) to a new MediaFileHelper.OpenSharedRead helper using FileShare.ReadWrite | Delete. Recycle-bin ownership marker + file-browser TOCTOU re-validation + timestamp width fix (from PR #11) + lazy legacy-adoption gate + zero-byte marker. New Settings: 'Pause fixes when the bin reaches N GB' size cap and 'Reset scheduled task' button (FixTaskSeeded flag makes ScheduleMigrator seed once instead of fighting the user on every restart). Duplicate detection rework with a per-pair confidence ladder (Exact 1.00 / Identified 0.90 / Heuristic 0.70) plus two hard vetoes (title-token Jaccard, runtime delta) that kill the GitHub #3 Futurama-specials false-positive class.

Fixes
- GitHub #3 - duplicate false positives on distinct files sharing an episode metadata slot.
- GitHub #12 - container CPU/RAM cards showed HOST numbers; now read cgroup v2 -> v1 first and fall through to /proc only when unbounded.
- GitHub #6 + #12-SMART - Linux SMART reported Unknown forever on drives whose libraries live on a partition; now walks partition -> disk via lsblk.
- ArtworkFixer clears the item's ImageInfos BEFORE deleting the file on disk so /Items/{id}/Images/Primary stops 404-ing after a corrupt-artwork sweep.
- Dry-run is now airtight: MissingSubtitleFixer no longer queries external subtitle providers under dry-run (was leaking which files exist and burning provider quota).
- Field report A1: default-threaded ffmpeg pinned every core on a 1-2 vCPU Docker VM and locked up SSH. Threads default to max(1, ProcessorCount/2).
- Field reports A9/A10: reworded 'original kept in recycle bin' and dry-run preview action text so users stop reading it as 'MediaDash is hoarding files'.
- Field report B1: sidecars now follow the primary file after a successful move.
- Field report B4: subtitles in Subtitles/ or Subs/ subfolders next to media are detected.
- Field report D2: MissingSubtitle now runs before Transcode so subtitles land before an encode that would rename-orphan them.
- NfoScanner no longer flags valid metadata as corrupt on missing per-Actor extensions or trailing text after </movie>.
- OrphanCleanupScanner: unrelated adjacent folders no longer treated as orphans; scanners emitting non-video paths opt out of scoped-delete so stale rows don't sit forever.
- EmbeddedCoverArtScanner: no longer flags every non-trivial AVI as corrupt.
- SmartHealth probe: no longer stuck on 'Checking SMART status...' forever on probe crash; PowerShell reliability-counter fallback no longer silently misses on trailing whitespace in FriendlyName.
- RecycleBin cross-volume move: .mediadash.tmp staging file is cleaned up when a move throws mid-way.
- LibraryMonitor: ReportFileSystemChanged now fires for both source and destination on move so cached ImageInfo drops.

Privacy
- Anonymous community-stats install ID is now month-rotated: SHA-256(salt || Jellyfin SystemId || year-month), never stored on disk. Prior persistent UUID was stronger linkability than APP/GDPR tolerates for 'aggregate community stats'.

Duplicates - new config
- DuplicateAutoFixConfidence (default 0.80): under Automatic mode, only pairs at or above this confidence are auto-queued.
- DuplicateTitleJaccardVeto (default 0.40): kills pairs whose filename title tokens overlap less than this.
- DuplicateRuntimeVetoPct (default 15%): kills pairs whose runtimes differ by more than this.
- New file_hashes cache table and Confidence column on issues (idempotent migration to schema v4).

Still one binary for both Jellyfin 10.11 and 12.0.

Full-scanner community stats, on-by-default opt-in, and first-run wizard layout polish. Dashboard's fix-completion popup and redownload banner now survive a plugin reload.

Features
- Community stats now cover every scanner MediaDash ships. 8 new scanners added to the payload, backend schema, and public views (Ungrouped, LargeTrickplay, SubtitleFonts, OrphanedDebris, CorruptNfo, HeavyTranscode, FailedTranscode, EmbeddedCoverArt) alongside the existing 10.
- Community stats default flipped from off to on for new installs. Existing installs are unchanged; their persisted AnalyticsEnabled value wins. The first-run wizard shows the checkbox pre-ticked; untick in Settings -> Safety at any time to opt out.
- Dashboard's LastFixRun (fix-completion popup) and RedownloadWarnings (Overview banner) are now persisted to the plugin DB via a write-through wrapper. Previously both dropped on every plugin reload, so a mid-day restart made the popup or banner vanish. Rehydrated on plugin start.
- README's community-impact table, docs/index.html impact section, and the monthly-stats GitHub Actions workflow now render rows for all 18 scanner types. docs/PRIVACY.md field table extended to match; opt-out language rewritten throughout.
- Docs screenshots (overview, issues, history, settings) regenerated against the current UI with Blender open-movie sample data - no personal filenames or hostnames.

Bug fixes
- First-run wizard "Skip walkthrough" now mints the anonymous install UUID when analytics is enabled. Previously, skipping the wizard left the ID empty and the reporter silently no-op'd, so an on-by-default install that never completed the walkthrough never actually contributed a single row.
- Wizard step 5 (Oversized files): "Skip HDR files" now sits to the right of "Preferred GPU" in a two-column flex row instead of stacked below the description. Both controls align to the same height.
- Wizard step 8 (Language cleanup): the mdChipInput language pickers no longer sit taller than the emby-select controls next to them. Same 46px height rule that already applied on the Settings tab now applies inside the wizard too.
- Wizard step 2 (Libraries): the "Check library access" button now uses the plugin's mdActionBtn class (rounded pill, primary accent, 44px tall) instead of Jellyfin's raw raised-button styling. Matches the rest of the plugin.
- Wizard step 16 (Community stats): intro copy no longer starts with "Off by default -" and now lists every scanner in the "What's sent" panel.

Reclaim totals now match across the plugin, heavy-transcode fixer works on well-encoded sources, SMART shows correctly on unprivileged Linux, and the History tab lets you slice failures by reason.

Features
- History tab's Failed filter now surfaces a "search by reason" dropdown listing the distinct failure reasons in your history with a count each (Permission denied, I/O error, Cross-device link, File no longer exists, etc.). Selecting one narrows the list; switching the top-level chip clears it.
- SMART pill on the Overview drives now shows a specific hint when smartctl fails due to permissions on Linux: setcap 'cap_sys_rawio+ep' $(which smartctl) for native installs, --cap-add=SYS_RAWIO --device=... for Docker.

Bug fixes
- Overview "Reclaimed since install" and History tab's summary + per-library chart now show the same number. History was summing the paginated 500-row window client-side while Overview summed the entire history server-side, causing the mismatch (e.g. 599 GB vs 8.1 GB). New /History/Stats endpoint aggregates over all history server-side; both panels source the total from it.
- Heavy-transcode / failed-transcode fixes no longer refuse to swap when the re-encoded file is slightly larger than the original. Those fix types exist for direct-play compatibility, not disk savings â€” the size gate is now Quality-only, with a 30% hard cap on the transcode types to guard against misconfigured encode settings.
- SMART pills now appear on library drives on Linux. Library-drive detection was using Path.GetPathRoot which always returns "/" on Linux â€” no library drive was ever flagged, so the SMART probe never ran there. Now uses the deepest-matching mount point via FindDriveForPath.
- smartctl exit_status is now honoured. Non-zero exit (permission denied, unsupported device, no SMART support) returns Unknown with the actual smartctl error message, instead of being mis-interpreted as "self-assessment FAILED".

Post-1.0.2 UX polish: inline access probes, better Overview labels, orphan-cleanup cross-volume fallback.

Features
- New "Test read / write access" buttons under Settings â†’ Libraries and Settings â†’ Recycle bin. Results render inline next to each library (green âœ“ readable + writable, or red âœ— with the specific error in a hover tooltip). Same probe as the first-run wizard, re-runnable any time.
- Libraries scoping list now shows every library type MediaDash can scan (movies, TV, music, audiobooks, books, comics, mixed) with a small type label next to each. Previously filtered to movies + TV only, hiding music / books / audiobooks even though every scanner has covered those since 0.9.
- Overview "Reclaimed since install" panel labels replace the older "Space saved to date" phrasing; per-library chart header matches.

Bug fixes
- OrphanCleanupFixer no longer errors out with "Invalid cross-device link" when a Jellyfin metadata folder (e.g. /var/lib/jellyfin/data/collections/*) is recycled and the recycle bin lives on a different volume. Directory.Move now falls back to the verified copy â†’ rename â†’ delete-source helper the file path uses.
- Errors tab no longer flashes / clears / closes user-expanded <details> when a new error arrives. loadErrors fingerprints the response (source + creation timestamp + count) and only re-renders when the entry set actually changes.
- Redundant "Where the savings are" bar section removed from Overview. The reclaim panel legend has shown the same per-type bytes breakdown since 1.0.2.

Follow-up polish on 1.0.1: fewer noisy issues, sharper reclaim numbers, more control over dashboards banners.

Features
- Trickplay scanner has a configurable minimum-size threshold (Settings â†’ Trickplay space savings). Default 10 MB filters out per-clip trickplay folders that swamp libraries with many short videos; 0 disables the threshold and flags every convertible folder.
- Recycle-bin size-warning threshold is now user-configurable (Settings â†’ Recycle bin). Default 10 GB matches the old hardcoded value; 0 disables the banner.
- Recycle-bin cross-volume warning dismiss button now persists across browser sessions (localStorage). Other banners stay session-scoped because their conditions self-clear.

Bug fixes
- Overview "Space you could reclaim" panel now shows reclaimable bytes per issue type (with the file count as a muted parenthetical), and the donut is sized by bytes instead of by count so the visual is proportional to actual reclaim. Types with zero savings (Ungrouped, MissingSubtitles, Stale) are filtered out â€” they belong on the Issues tab, not the space-reclaim summary.
- Progress bar wrap on the masthead now spans the full width of the scan-state line above it (was previously capped at 36em).

Post-1.0 UI polish and a recycle-bin config regression fix.

Bug fixes
- RecycleBin path no longer requires library-adjacency. Users can point the bin at any writable location (e.g. `/mnt/media/.mediadash-recycle` as a sibling of the library for cross-volume-free moves). Only OS-reserved roots (/etc, /bin, /usr, Windows System32, etc.) are refused.
- Errors tab: badge no longer shows a stale count (e.g. "691") after the tab has been cleared. The periodic status poll now delegates to loadErrors() when the user is on the Errors tab, so badge + list update from the same fetch.
- Issues tab: badge is now sourced from the actual issue list length, so "999+" no longer disagrees with the visible cards.
- Overview issue-shortcut cards now show reclaimable space (bytes / MB / GB) as the primary number, with the file count as a subtitle. Types with no space-savings info still show the raw count.
- Progress bar activity text now spans the full width of the scan-state line above it (was capped at 36em).
- Removed the second empty "Subtitles" settings card that appeared post-1.0 (SubtitleFonts controls are already folded into the SubtitleLanguage card).
- "Collapse all" / "Expand all" button on Settings now truthfully reflects what a click will do: it excludes force-collapsed Off-mode tasks from the state check, and hides itself entirely when nothing on the page is togglable.

Features
- Full media coverage on Jellyfin 10.11 and 12.0 from one binary: movies, TV, music, audiobooks, books, comics.
- Ungrouped-media grouper and Corrupt-artwork scanner now fully wired into the UI (types, settings card, per-type mode).
- ISO 639-1 (2-letter) language tags fold to ISO 639-2 via CultureInfo so "en" matches ["eng"] and single-language audio tracks stop getting flagged for removal.
- Opportunistic 15-minute fix scheduling with idle deferral; automatic migration from legacy DailyTrigger on first boot.
- Post-Jellyfin-12 upgrade cleanup that sweeps orphaned trickplay folders on first launch.
- Book (EPUB / PDF / MOBI / AZW3) and comic (CBZ / CBR / CB7) integrity probes.
- Corrupt-artwork, orphan-cleanup, trickplay-optimize, embedded-cover-art, heavy-transcode, failed-transcode and NFO-integrity scanners.
- File browser tab (rename / move / delete / upload inside library boundaries, deletes go to the recycle bin).
- Per-GPU picker + hardware-accelerated re-encoding (AMF / NVENC / QSV / VideoToolbox) with automatic software fallback.
- Errors tab with copy-diagnostics-for-bug-report button.

Bug fixes
- RecycleBin cross-volume moves verify copy size before deleting the source (no more silent data loss on truncated writes).
- MoveToBin folder names carry a per-batch GUID so same-millisecond recycles no longer collide.
- FileBrowser rename / move now return 409 on concurrent-target creation instead of silently overwriting.
- Upload endpoint rejects oversized bodies via Content-Length pre-flight before any disk I/O; 50 GB per-file cap.
- LibraryGuard refuses paths whose ancestor chain contains a symlink or NTFS junction.
- RecycleBinPath must sit inside the plugin data dir or a configured library; OS-reserved roots refused.
- SweepOrphanSidecars enumerates with reparse-point skip and re-checks each candidate before delete.
- IsSimpleName refuses Windows reserved names (CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1-9, LPT1-9) and trailing dot / space.
- RelocateIssuePaths uses COLLATE NOCASE on the boundary match so sibling issues re-point correctly after case-varying moves on Windows.
- PlayabilityFixer re-verify is reason-driven (audio-kind files no longer recycled on "no-audio" false positives; size-truncated files now actually removed).
- TrackFixer.IsSelfReferentialSubtitle normalises both paths via Path.GetFullPath so legacy relative-path issue rows can't trick the guard.
- MediaSorterFixer cross-volume detection works on Linux (was previously blind because Path.GetPathRoot returns "/").
- MissingSubtitleFixer catches TaskCanceledException from provider network stalls without aborting the whole fix run.
- smartctl / nvidia-smi / df invocations use ArgumentList (no shell tokenization); absolute-path resolution on Linux where possible.
- WMI drive-letter validated before WQL interpolation.
- BulkUpdateOpenIssueStatus chunks at 500 params; controller caps requests at 50 k IDs.
- SmartHealthProbe stdout and stderr drained concurrently before WaitForExit (no more pipe-buffer deadlocks on large SMART payloads).
- Diagnostics ring buffer dedup keys off a hash of the pre-truncation message; entries are replaced (not mutated) so concurrent Recent() callers can't observe torn reads.
- AssSubtitleFile.Parse caps input at 100 MB to prevent OOM on malformed sidecars.
- Wizard i18n guard relaxed to Math.min so partial locale translations override index-by-index instead of falling back entirely to English.
- Retention slider in Settings now runs to 365 days (matched the wizard, no more silent 90-day cap on save).
- Update banner no longer fires on 0.0.0.0 dev builds.
- AnalyticsEnabled default flipped to false to match every "off by default" string in the UI.
- Task-active count derived from FIX_TYPES.length (previously hardcoded "of 15", now correct for all 18 fix types).
- Obsolete ScheduledFixTime config field removed.

Bug-fix bundle over 0.9.9.3.

Duplicate detector no longer flags different files with a shared prefix as duplicates. Replaced the trailing-tag whitelist (which kept missing new suffix combos users reported) with file-name-based edition detection: any variation in the filename between two TMDb-matched files yields a different edition key when 'Treat editions as duplicates' is off. Covers 100% of possible suffix combinations. Byte-identical copies with the same filename still group as duplicates. Regression: 'StarWarsCloneWars2003 - Connecting the Dots.mkv' vs 'StarWarsCloneWars2003 - Bridging the Saga.mkv' â€” now stays as two separate entries.

Jellyfin sidecar files/folders are skipped by the Duplicate scanner before grouping â€” no more 'theme.mp3 in show1/ is a duplicate of theme.mp3 in show2/' reports. Covers theme/themevideo/poster/backdrop/logo/etc plus extras subfolders (extras, trailers, behind the scenes, deleted scenes, featurettes, ...) and per-item extras suffixes in both compact and spaced form ('-behindthescenes' and '- Behind the scenes'). Reference: https://jellyfin.org/docs/general/server/media/movies/#extras

Dismiss button on issue cards renamed to 'Ignore this' â€” the existing behaviour already blocks that file from re-reporting, the old label was just confusing.

New: notification badges on Issues (open count, cyan), History (failed rows count, amber), and Errors tabs (unchanged).

Version scheme: feature.feature.feature.bugfix â€” fourth digit increments for hotfixes.

New Overview banner warns when a MediaDash re-encode gets undone by something external (typically Sonarr/Radarr redownloading a "too-small" file whose size dropped below the quality profile minimum, but also fires on manual recycle-bin restores or backup-restore overwrites).

Detection is evidence-based, not guessed: at the end of every scan MediaDash walks the last 30 days of successful non-dry-run history entries, and for each one where the ORIGINAL is still preserved in the recycle bin, compares the file currently at the same path against the recycled original. If the current file is within 10% of the original size â€” i.e. the same rough size we shrank down â€” the shrunk copy has been replaced. Only paths meeting that concrete size-match trigger the warning. False positives are limited to genuine restores, which are also worth surfacing.

The red banner shows the filename, the shrunk-to size, the current size, and the fix date. Dismissable per browser session; reappears on the next scan if the condition still holds.

Two fixes and a reclaim.

VAAPI hardware encodes now pass -rc_mode VBR to hevc_vaapi / h264_vaapi / av1_vaapi. Mesa VAAPI's default rate-control is CQP, which ignores -b:v/-maxrate and picks a QP that routinely produces output LARGER than a modest-bitrate source â€” the "the re-encoded file would be larger than the original, so the original was kept" retry loop that some AMD iGPU users saw every 30-70 minutes on the same file. VBR honours -b:v as the target and -maxrate as the ceiling, so the encoder actually stays under the requested bitrate.

Orphan sidecar sweep: at the end of every fix run (right after the recycle bin purge), MediaDash now walks each library root and deletes any *.mediadash.tmp*, *.mediadash.new*, mediadash.tmp.*, or mediadash.new.* file it finds. These are leftovers from a hard-killed encode (SIGKILL, container restart, Jellyfin crash) where the C# finally block that normally deletes them never ran. Deleted-count + reclaimed-bytes go into Jellyfin's log.

FfmpegExecutor now sweeps for orphaned MediaDash ffmpeg processes before spawning a new encode. Linux only (reads /proc/<pid>/cmdline; Windows/macOS would need extra deps for a very rare failure mode). Any ffmpeg whose command line contains a mediadash.tmp or mediadash.new marker is killed with SIGKILL and its sidecar output file is deleted. Prevents the "two ffmpegs writing to the same output" scenario after a plugin hot-reload or a Jellyfin restart mid-encode. Also cleans up the interleaved-bytes .tmp file that would otherwise sit on disk until the next fix run on the same source overwrote it.

Manual fix runs now pause instead of bailing when someone starts watching. Click "Run fixes now", the queue drains as before, but if the pause-on-playback check trips between files the run pauses (with an amber banner: "Paused: someone is watching. Click 'Ignore activity' to resume anyway.") and re-checks every 30 seconds. When the viewer stops or you hit the Ignore activity button, the run resumes from where it stopped. Scheduled runs keep the previous behaviour (break on activity, next 15-minute tick tries again). The Ignore flag only applies to the current run â€” a fresh Run fixes now click brings the pause behaviour back.

Fix the "Fix run finished with failures" popup firing on every page load. The first-poll guard checked prevFinishedAt !== undefined but lastStatus starts as null, which short-circuited prevFinishedAt to null (not undefined) â€” so opening the plugin page always fired an alert if the most-recent completed run had any failures, even while a new run was still going. The alert now only fires when a poll's FinishedAtUtc actually changes from a prior poll.

Fix cascade after 0.9.3 hit real prod hardware. Track-remux fixer now uses the same hash-fallback sidecar name as the transcode fixer (v0.9.2 shipped it for one path, not both) â€” long-UTF-8 filenames (Cyrillic/CJK) no longer fail with ffmpeg "Error opening output" on Linux NAME_MAX. Free-disk-space check now looks at the actual mount containing the file via RecycleBin.FindDriveForPath, not the root filesystem â€” LXC/Docker setups where /mnt/media is a large bind-mount but / is a tiny rootfs no longer get false "Not enough free disk space" bailouts on 30-60 GB BDRemuxes. QualityScanner is less trigger-happy: dropped the container-level bitrate fallback (was flagging remuxes with big lossless audio as "video too fat"), and added a 15%-of-file-size minimum-savings gate so HEVC->HEVC recompression at close bitrates doesn't burn a 20-minute encode only for the fixer to abort with "the re-encoded file would be larger than the original". TrackFixer's error truncation matches TranscodeFixer now â€” keeps the ffmpeg-error tail (where the real reason lives), not the head.

Transcode fix now actually uses the GPU. v0.9.2 shipped without the hardware-encoder path wired in â€” the UseHardwareEncoder toggle had no effect and every re-encode ran on the CPU via libx265. This release wires the hw path through and adds full VAAPI support (device auto-picked from /dev/dri/renderD* or Jellyfin's VaapiDevice, with format=nv12,hwupload / scale_vaapi in the filter chain). When Jellyfin's own HardwareAccelerationType is unset, the plugin now autodetects: NVIDIA â†’ NVENC, any Linux DRM device (Intel/AMD iGPU or dGPU) â†’ VAAPI, Windows â†’ AMF (or QSV for Intel iGPUs), macOS â†’ VideoToolbox, and falls back to libx265 only when no GPU is present. Any hardware failure still retries with software so no encode gets stuck. Settings page tidy-up: 'Thorough playability check' no longer has the oversized inset box beside the disposal dropdown; Issues tab drops the redundant 'Show' type filter (the count pills already do that) and moves the filename search onto the same row.

Groups TV episodes into per-show folders and movie franchises (>=2 siblings) into shared folders using Jellyfin's identified metadata. Fixes false-positive duplicate detection when Jellyfin derives Movie.Name from a folder (name-fallback keys now include the filename; also tightened for Book and Audio, with a required runtime for audio). Fixes transcode failure on filenames near Linux's 255-byte limit (Cyrillic/CJK) via hash-based sidecar names. Failed fixes that mean 'file no longer exists' or 'nothing left to remove' now auto-clear from the queue instead of retrying every 15 minutes. Move-style fixers now update sibling issues in the DB so they don't fail with 'no longer exists' after a rename. Issues tab: per-type total pills, 'Try to play' button on Playability cards, Duplicate cards show keeper location. ffmpeg error output now shows the tail (where the actual error is) instead of the codec startup banner.

versions.changelog: # 🚀 A New Foundation for File Transformation File Transformation **3.0.0.0** is a major overhaul of how the plugin integrates with Jellyfin. The transformation system has been rebuilt around standard ASP.NET Core middleware, removing much of the version-specific runtime patching that File Transformation previously relied on. Alongside **Jellyfin 12 support**, this release drops support for **Jellyfin 10.10.7** and lays a much more maintainable foundation for future Jellyfin releases. > ## 🙌 Huge thanks to @4eh5xitv6787h645ebv > > A massive part of this release is thanks to **@4eh5xitv6787h645ebv**, who took on the major overhaul of File Transformation's core architecture in PR #58. > > The move away from the old Harmony/MonoMod-based interception system to standard ASP.NET Core middleware is a significant piece of work. It not only makes File Transformation substantially easier to maintain, but also resolves an entire class of compatibility problems that caused the plugin to malfunction or be disabled on certain Jellyfin versions and platforms (#20, #35, #62, #64, #70, #71). > > This is far more than a small patch or isolated feature - it fundamentally improves the foundation the plugin is built on. A huge thank you for the time and effort that went into it. ## ✨ New Features * Added support for **Jellyfin 12** and the newer Jellyfin server architecture (#34). * Replaced the previous Harmony/MonoMod-based web interception system with standard ASP.NET Core `IStartupFilter` middleware (PR #58, @4eh5xitv6787h645ebv). * Added support for unregistering transformations through `PluginInterface.RemoveTransformation(Guid)`, allowing dependent plugins to cleanly remove transformations when required. * Added support for synthesising virtual files for registered transformation paths, restoring support for plugins such as Plugin Pages where the underlying file doesn't physically exist. * Added ETag generation and `304 Not Modified` support for transformed content. * Added Brotli and gzip recompression of transformed responses for remote clients. * Added automatic MIME type detection for virtual transformed files. ## 🛠️ Improvements * Removed platform-specific DLL extraction and version-specific Jellyfin shims. * Removed dependencies on Harmony, MonoMod and Prometheus from the core transformation pipeline. * Improved compatibility across Jellyfin versions and platforms by moving the transformation system onto standard ASP.NET Core APIs (#20, #35, #62, #64). * Added per-transformation error isolation so a failure in one plugin's transformation won't prevent other transformations from running. * Made transformation registration, removal and execution thread-safe. * Added regex caching and timeout protection for transformation matching. * Improved handling of `Accept-Encoding`, including proper quality-value (`q`) parsing. * Improved LAN detection for IPv6-mapped IPv4 addresses. * Improved proxy caching behaviour by correctly setting `Vary: Accept-Encoding`. * Reworked HTTP handling to use a shared `HttpClient` with appropriate timeouts. * Hardened named-pipe transformations with timeouts, size limits, EOF handling and improved resource cleanup. ## 🪲 Bug Fixes * Fixed a class of failures where Harmony/MonoMod runtime patching could cause File Transformation to malfunction or be automatically disabled on startup (#20, #35, #62, #64, #71). * Fixed #70 where transformations could attempt to use a disposed `IServiceProvider` after Jellyfin restarted, resulting in `500` responses across the web UI. * Fixed transformed content potentially retaining stale trailing bytes when a transformation produced a shorter result than the original response. * Fixed failures in one transformation potentially breaking the entire transformation pipeline. * Fixed potential `HttpClient` resource leaks. * Fixed named-pipe transformations being able to hang indefinitely or loop on zero-byte reads. * Fixed incorrect handling of disabled compression encodings such as `gzip;q=0`. * Fixed failed virtual-file transformations returning an empty successful response instead of reverting to the original `404`. * Improved middleware failure handling so the original response is served if transformation or recompression fails. ## 💻 Developer Compatibility The existing `PluginInterface.RegisterTransformation` API and registration payload remain compatible with previous releases, so plugins using a standard transformation callback **should not need to change how they register transformations**. There are, however, some changes to transformation execution that plugin developers should be aware of: * Added `PluginInterface.RemoveTransformation(Guid)`, allowing plugins to explicitly unregister a previously registered transformation. * Assembly callbacks still receive the same payload and are expected to return the transformed content as a `string`. * Invalid or failed assembly callbacks now **fail safely rather than falling through to another configured callback mechanism**. Plugins should ensure their callback assembly, class and method names are valid. * HTTP transformation callbacks must now return a **successful HTTP status code**. Non-success responses are treated as a failed transformation rather than using the response body as transformed content. * HTTP callbacks now have a **15 second timeout**. * Named-pipe callbacks now have connection/error handling and a **50 MB maximum response size**. * Failed transformations now leave the original response untouched rather than potentially replacing it with invalid or partial output. These changes are intended to make transformations significantly safer and more predictable, but plugins relying on the previous fallback or error behaviour should review their integrations when updating. ## ⚠️ Compatibility * **Jellyfin 10.10.7 is no longer supported.** * Added support for **Jellyfin 12** and its newer server architecture (#34). * Users remaining on Jellyfin 10.10.7 will need to stay on an earlier File Transformation release until they upgrade Jellyfin. * Removed legacy Harmony/MonoMod runtime patching and version-specific Jellyfin shims. * File Transformation now relies on standard ASP.NET Core middleware rather than patching Jellyfin internals, providing a much more stable base for future Jellyfin versions. ## Contributors * 4eh5xitv6787h645ebv ## ❤️ Support If you enjoy using my Jellyfin plugins and want to support the time that goes into building, maintaining, and improving them, you can do so on [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/IAmParadox27). Thank you for using the plugins and being part of the community.

versions.changelog:
This update brings together 2.0.10.0 and 2.0.11.0 from the beta channel.

If you use the Live TV allow-list behind a reverse proxy: add the proxy to Known Proxies in Jellyfin's networking settings. Without that, every request through the proxy counts as coming from the proxy, and if its address is on your list, everyone gets in. The help text now says so.

Fixed: with Live TV set up on two or more providers, the guide never used your providers' XMLTV files. They were combined into one file that could not be read past the first provider, so the guide always fell back to the simpler per-channel listings and lost categories, ratings and the other details XMLTV carries. Each provider's file is now read on its own. If one provider's file is missing or broken, only that provider's channels fall back, and the others keep their full guide (found and fixed by dillardblom).

Fixed: when two providers used the same guide id for different channels, one of them got no guide, or showed the other provider's programmes. Guide ids are now matched per provider (reported by dillardblom).

Fixed: when your provider's XMLTV guide came through cut off part way, building the guide never finished. Each request for the EPG URL kept one CPU core busy until Jellyfin gave up, and the guide stayed empty. A broken file now falls back to fetching the guide per channel, as it already did when the file was missing, and no programme is listed twice (by dillardblom).

Fixed: with Dispatcharr mode on, every sync worker logged in to Dispatcharr at the same time when a sync started. Dispatcharr's login limit refused most of them, and those workers fell back to the Xtream API for the first minutes. There is now one login shared by all of them, and it waits its turn like every other request (reported by dillardblom).

This update brings together 2.0.2.0 to 2.0.9.0 from the beta channel.

If you use Live TV with the Native Tuner only, open the Live TV tab after updating and turn off the new "Publish Playlists" switch. It stays on for anyone who already had Live TV enabled, so an M3U tuner or TiviMate setup keeps working, but the native tuner does not need it.

Fixed: Request Delay now limits how fast the plugin talks to your provider in total. Each parallel worker used to apply it separately, so with Sync Parallelism at 10 and the default of 50 ms up to 200 requests a second could go out, enough for some providers to block your IP. It is now one shared gap per provider: 50 ms means at most 20 a second. When the provider says it is getting too many requests, every request to it waits. A first sync of a large library takes longer as a result; if your provider allows more, lower Request Delay. Setting it to 0 is no longer saved as 50 (reported by dillardblom).

Fixed: a single unreadable value from your provider, such as an empty value where a number belongs, no longer makes content disappear. It could blank a series' title, plot and TMDB id, drop every episode of a series, or make a whole category fail to sync. Such values are now ignored or read as 0, and an item whose ID cannot be read is skipped with a warning while the rest syncs normally (reported by foXaCe).

Fixed: changing Folder Mode, or moving a category to another folder, no longer leaves every moved item in your library twice. The old copies are removed even beyond the orphan safety limit, as long as the item only moved to another category folder; anything that actually disappeared is still protected by the limit. Moved items lose their watched status, because Jellyfin sees a new folder as a new item (reported in andreadegiovine's fork).

Fixed: when orphan cleanup removes a movie or series, the NFO and poster the plugin wrote are removed with it, so the folder no longer stays behind. Files you added yourself, such as subtitles or your own NFO, are kept, and so is the folder (idea from andreadegiovine).

Fixed: with "Group movies with the same TMDB id" on, a film whose request the provider missed no longer ends up in a folder of its own. It is held back and picked up on the next sync. Films already split this way stay split; to fix them, use Delete Movies Library in the Danger Zone and sync again (reported by andreadegiovine).

New: with "Fallback to Year-Free Lookup" on, an unmatched movie is also searched with the year of the provider's release date and with its original title, which helps when the title carries the wrong year or is in another language. A search without a year is checked against the release date, so it cannot pick a remake. A match found by the year-free retry is now remembered for later syncs, for movies and series. Movies already in your library keep their folders (idea from philx17).

New: "Publish Playlists" on the Live TV tab. The M3U and Catch-up M3U URLs contain your Xtream username and password and can be reached without a Jellyfin login. They are now only served while this switch is on, and it is off when you enable Live TV from now on. The EPG URL and channel logos are not affected (proposed by dillardblom).

New: "Restrict These URLs To" limits the Live TV URLs to the addresses you list, one per line. Leave it empty for no restriction. If you use it, include 127.0.0.1 and ::1, since Jellyfin fetches channel logos itself, and behind a reverse proxy add the proxy to Known Proxies in Jellyfin's networking settings first (written by dillardblom).

Fixed: a Live TV category, channel or logo address with & in it no longer shows as & or breaks (reported by TheBazeman).

Categories load their items again on Jellyfin 12 (#117).

Jellyfin 12 stops accepting the legacy `X-Emby-Token` request header. Two of the configuration page fetch sites still sent it: the Live TV category loader and the Series / VOD content loader. Both now send `Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=` instead, which Jellyfin 12's `CustomAuthentication` middleware expects. The Test connection button was never affected and still works as before. Two-line header swap in `config.js`, no server-side change.

## Features
- Republishes 12.2.3.0, whose download did not match its checksum and could not install.

## Features
- Import Spotify playlists exported with Exportify, one playlist as CSV or all of them as a ZIP.

versions.changelog: 10.11.11.0 - Want to watch gains three options, all off by default and all requiring the arrived-titles playlist (contributed by David Rappo, @rappo, in PR 21): the home row can lead with the titles already on your playlist, a title comes off the playlist once it is watched (a series once every episode is played), and a movie or series page gets a bookmark button among its own. Plugin rows are reachable with a TV remote's D-pad. Not interested, off by default, lets each user hide a title from their own Web UI pages without hiding it for anyone else. A user with a parental rating limit sees the Web UI sections narrowed to the titles that limit allows, rather than none of them. The home Discover row, the Want to watch row, and the item page rows each have a placement setting; existing settings carry over. The Gaps Report's toolbar is grouped by what each control acts on, every header has a select-all, a line above the list says how many rows the filters hide, and Add to TODO is now Add to watchlist. The report is usable at phone width, and the settings page has collapsible sections, a search, and better screen reader support. A new scheduled task, Prune gaps from deleted items, takes deleted library items out of the report: a gap they were the only source of is removed, and one with other sources moves to the next. It has no default schedule; it waits for a running scan, and a second scan waits for the first. Recommendation groups link to the owned title they came from. Books get an OpenLibrary id field and albums and artists a Discogs id field in the metadata editor, with a link on the item's page; a dedicated OpenLibrary or Discogs plugin takes over when installed. Links are built from each title's ids when the report loads, so a link plugin installed later applies everywhere. The report takes far less memory and disk (on a library with 83,000 gaps, about 1.6 GB down to 200 MB in memory and 245 MB down to 131 MB on disk), loads in about half the time, and is written far less often during scans and where-to-watch lookups. Existing reports convert on first load; a report saved by this version cannot be read by an earlier one, so going back shows an empty report until its next scan.

10.11.10.0 - The Maintenance section has a Fulfillment queue for an administrator who fetches titles by hand. It folds every user's TODO list into one row per title, sorted by how many people still want it, names who is still waiting, and shows the streaming-service icons as soon as the queue opens, with the same links a TODO row already has. Mark fetched closes the title for every requester in one action, and Verify all checks the queue against the library and closes a title you already have, however it arrived. With Everyone's watchlist on (off by default), that same household list is a Discover source and leads the Discover view of every domain it has entries for. Send to the acquisition stack is done from the Gaps Report. The report's Send action has a quality profile picker, filled from the stack's own profile list and preselecting the profile you configured, so an older title the default profile cannot find a release for can still be sent. The report's My TODO list popup is gone; the Fulfillment queue is where an administrator sees every list. The report's multi-select bar can Acquire, Request, or Resolve a checked batch (Resolve applies one shared note), alongside Mint and Add to TODO. An administrator can manage another user's want-to-watch list. With "Want to watch: move arrived titles into a playlist" on, a title that is in the library moves into that user's own Jellyfin playlist the next time it is verified, so it shows up in every client. The playlist is named Want to Watch unless you change it, and only a real file counts as arrived. Amazon and web-search links for a book or album include the author or artist, on the report, the Web UI, and the Fulfillment queue. TMDB lists, Trakt lists, and OpenLibrary subjects are set with the same chip pickers the other curated sources use. A book's dialog loads its description from OpenLibrary when you open it. Studio pages, off by default, add a Missing from the studio row of that studio's movies you do not own, on the list page you open from a movie's studio credit. A library that sets a metadata fetcher order keeps TVmaze in the series check. TVmaze is not a Jellyfin metadata fetcher, so it is always asked and ranked last.

10.11.9.0 - Mind the Gaps now reaches into Jellyfin's own pages through an experimental, opt-in Web UI, with a master switch and one toggle per surface in settings, all off by default. A person's page lists what they made that you do not own, a movie or series page suggests titles like it that you are missing, an artist's page lists the albums you do not have, and a book page or an author's own page lists more by the same author. The home page can show a Discover row of the recommendations your scans found from titles you own and from lists that are public by nature (TMDB lists, Trakt lists, and TMDB's own feeds), never from a watchlist, wantlist, favorites, or a personal list. Click a card for a detail dialog with TMDB's synopsis, genres, runtime, rating, a trailer link, and a link to the title's JustWatch page, then send it to Radarr or Sonarr with the quality profile you pick; the dialog and the card grids can be driven from a keyboard or a TV remote. A user with a parental rating limit is shown none of these sections. With Want to watch turned on, every card carries a bookmark that adds the title to your own list, and the home page can show a Want to watch row of what you have listed and do not yet own. The TODO list is now kept per user, in the plugin's data folder, and removed when the user is deleted; the first administrator to open the old shared list takes it over, and an administrator can switch the report's TODO to everyone's lists to see and manage them. The Gaps Report loads faster: it fetches one tab at a time as slim rows, fetches a row's details only when you open it, revalidates what it already holds instead of downloading it again, and loads its script and stylesheet as separately cached files; the saved report is stored as one file per domain, and an existing report is converted automatically. A row shows up to two streaming-service icons, following your provider and monetization filters and wearing the service's logo (a service TMDB lists as several providers, such as a "with Ads" tier, shows as one icon and one provider filter entry), and clicking them opens the title's TMDB watch page. Gaps left behind by a source you have since removed or turned off are pruned on every scan, and a Prune stale gaps button under Maintenance does it right away. A TMDB list that cannot be read, such as a private one, no longer stops the other lists from being scanned, filling in a large library's series content is done in batches, and the scan log says how long each source took. New, and off by default: the report and the Web UI can load their posters, covers, and streaming-service logos through your server instead of each browser fetching them from TMDB and the other providers. Turn on "Keep the pages' images on this server" in the new Images section of settings; the server fetches each image once, from a fixed list of provider hosts only, keeps it under its cache folder, and sends the browser on to the provider whenever it cannot serve one, and a "Trim the image cache" scheduled task keeps the cache to the size you set (500 MB by default).

10.11.8.0 - The Gaps Report is reorganized around your library's domains: Movies, Shows, Music, and Books are now the primary tabs, each badged with its own gap count, with Set completion, Creator works, and Discover scoped underneath as a view you pick per domain, so only the active domain's data is loaded at a time. A Compact view toggle switches to a denser layout. Click a title to expand its detail in place: the overview, where to watch, and (outside Compact view) every information and action button tile inline instead of opening separate popovers; collapsed, the same actions live behind three icon popovers on the row, and a collapsed title's own browser tooltip shows its overview with no click at all. The toolbar is split into a filter row and an action row, and the settings page is reorganized into one collapsible section per provider (TMDB, Trakt, MDBList, Discogs, OpenLibrary, TheTVDB, IMDb, JustWatch), each badged on or off, with a search box that opens whichever section matches. Four new TMDB feeds, Top Rated, Popular, Upcoming, and Now Playing, can be turned on individually under Discover, and Jellyfin 12.0 is now a supported target alongside 10.11, each release building and shipping its own ABI-matched package. Gaps now show real cover art for books (bibliography and subject lists), music (MusicBrainz discography and artist works), and series completion episodes (TMDB, TheTVDB, and TVmaze all supply a still where they have one) instead of a blank thumbnail, falling back to the placeholder rather than a broken-image icon when a cover fails to load; MDBList entries carry a poster and description like every other source. A creator's page can be trimmed further with a minimum TMDB vote count for a movie credit and a minimum episode count for a TV credit. The TODO list shows an image and release date per entry. Sending a whole-series gap to Sonarr from a filmography, recommendation, or favorites entry sends the series' own title rather than the name of whatever surfaced it, and a rejected Radarr, Sonarr, or Jellyseerr request shows the service's validation message instead of a raw response body.
